h1: The 6 Best Blue-Light-Filtering Monitor Privacy Screens, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Blue Light Privacy Screens: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 monitor privacy screens with blue-light filtering, scored on fit, glare reduction, pack value and size from 21.5 to 34 inches.
mainKeyword: blue light filtering monitor privacy screen
summary: The Peslv 2-Pack 24 inch privacy screen is the best buy for most desks, bundling privacy, glare reduction and blue-light filtering in a pair at a mid-range price. The 24 inch 2-pack with anti-glare is a close alternative, the 27 inch 2-pack covers larger panels, and the Mamol 34 inch is the only option for a curved ultrawide. The SightPro and the 21.5 inch filter are the single-screen budget picks.
intro: The first mistake buyers make with a privacy screen is measuring the diagonal and stopping there. A filter that is a quarter inch off in either direction either leaves a visible gap or overlaps the bezel, and neither looks or works right. Aspect ratio matters as much as the diagonal, which is why a 24 inch 16:9 filter will not fit a 24 inch 16:10 monitor.

This ranking covers six privacy screens that also filter blue light, from 21.5 inch single sheets to a curved 34 inch ultrawide. We reviewed the specifications and listings for size, aspect ratio, pack count, glare and scratch features and fit. We also state plainly that blue-light filtering is a modest comfort feature, not a medical treatment, and that every filter dims the screen somewhat.

products.name: Peslv [2-Pack] 24 Inch Privacy Screen, Eye Protection Anti Blue Light Glare Shield
products.verdict: A 24 inch 16:9 pair that bundles privacy, glare reduction and blue-light filtering at a fair price.
products.description:
The Peslv is a 2-pack of 24 inch, 16:9 privacy screens with blue-light filtering and a glare shield. It sits in the $50 to $100 bucket and suits dual-monitor desks or a spare for a second workstation.

It takes first place because it gets the three jobs a privacy filter must do into one product and gives you two of them. 24 inch 16:9 is the most common monitor size, so more people can use it without hunting for a fit. A pair works out cheaper per screen than buying singles, which helps when you run two monitors. Against the SightPro below it, you get a second filter and an explicit glare feature rather than privacy alone.

Buy it if you have a standard 24 inch widescreen monitor, or two. Check your monitor's exact dimensions first, because filters are sized to a specific width and height.

products.idealFor: Dual-monitor desks with standard 24 inch widescreen displays.
products.skipIf: Your monitor is 16:10 or a different diagonal.

products.name: [2 Pack] 24 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter, Anti Glare Blue Light
products.verdict: A second 24 inch pair that explicitly pairs anti-glare and blue-light filtering.
products.description:
This is another 2-pack of 24 inch, 16:9 privacy screens, with anti-glare and blue-light filtering. Its price bucket, $50 to $100, matches the Peslv.

It ranks second because the two are nearly identical on paper, and the Peslv simply wins on the clearer eye-protection and glare shield description. The anti-glare surface helps in bright offices and rooms with windows, where reflections are the main complaint with a glossy panel. A matte finish also softens fingerprints. The tradeoff against the Peslv is less detail on the listing and a less recognizable name.

It is a fine choice if the Peslv is out of stock or you want anti-glare as the headline. As with any filter, expect some reduction in brightness and sharpness.
products.idealFor: Bright offices where reflections are the main annoyance.
products.skipIf: You want the clearest feature description on the listing.

products.name: [2 Pack] 27 Inch Computer Monitor Privacy Screen, Blue Light Filter
products.verdict: A 27 inch 16:9 pair in the $25 to $50 bucket for larger monitors.
products.description:
This 2-pack covers 27 inch, 16:9 monitors with a blue-light filter and privacy filtering. It sits in the $25 to $50 bucket, which makes it good value for the size.

It ranks third because 27 inch monitors are common on home desks and the pair is priced under the 24 inch ones. The larger screen is where privacy matters most, since a bigger display is easier to see from the side, and where a pair is a real saving. The tradeoff is that bigger filters are harder to install bubble-free, and a larger sheet is more prone to creases in the mounting.

Buy it if you have a 27 inch 16:9 monitor, and measure it carefully. If your monitor has a different aspect ratio, this one will not fit.
pros: Lower price bucket than 24 inch pairs
cons: Bigger sheet is harder to fit
products.idealFor: Home desks with one or two 27 inch widescreen monitors.

products.name: Mamol 34 Inch Curved Computer Privacy Screen Filter, Anti Glare Blue Light
products.verdict: The only filter here for a 21:9 curved ultrawide, with anti-glare, blue-light and anti-scratch layers.
products.description:
The Mamol is a 34 inch privacy filter for 21:9 ultrawide monitors and is listed as curved-compatible. It adds blue-light filtering, anti-glare and anti-scratch properties, priced between $50 and $100.

Fourth place reflects its narrow audience, not a weakness. If you own a 34 inch curved ultrawide, nothing else on the list fits, and this one is the only option. Curved panels are the hard case for any filter, since a flat film has to bend to match the screen, so check that your monitor's curve is gentle enough. The anti-scratch layer is a useful bonus on a large, exposed screen.

Buy it if you have a 34 inch 21:9 ultrawide and want privacy at the office. Skip it for any other size.
products.idealFor: Owners of 34 inch curved ultrawide monitors.
products.skipIf: Your monitor is any other size or aspect ratio.

products.name: SightPro 24 Inch 16:9 Computer Privacy Screen Filter for Monitor
products.verdict: A single 24 inch 16:9 filter in the $25 to $50 bucket, for one-monitor desks.
products.description:
The SightPro is a single 24 inch, 16:9 privacy filter for monitors. It sits in the $25 to $50 bucket and is aimed at buyers with one screen.

It ranks fifth because the 2-packs give you a second filter at a similar total cost. The listing does not spell out a blue-light claim in the product name, so check the product page if blue-light filtering is your priority. The single-unit format is a plus if you only have one monitor and do not want a spare, and the SightPro name has been on the market for years.

It makes sense for a one-monitor desk where you want only privacy and do not need extras. If you have two screens, one of the 24 inch pairs is a better deal.

methodology.description: A filter that does not match your monitor is useless, so we scored size, aspect ratio and curved-screen support, and noted exact-fit requirements.

methodology.title: Feature set
methodology.description: We compared privacy, blue-light filtering, anti-glare and anti-scratch claims on each listing, and gave less credit where the listing did not confirm a feature.

methodology.title: Pack value
methodology.description: Two filters at a similar price give more value than one, which matters for dual-monitor desks. We compared pack counts against price buckets.

methodology.description: Every filter dims the screen and adds some softness. We favored designs that pair anti-glare with filtering without promising unrealistic clarity.

methodology.title: Installation ease
methodology.description: Large sheets are harder to fit bubble-free and curved screens add another challenge. We considered how forgiving each format is to install and remove.

whatMatters.factor: Exact monitor size and aspect ratio
whatMatters.detail: Privacy filters are cut to a specific width and height, so the diagonal alone is not enough. A 24 inch 16:9 filter is about 20.9 inches wide and 11.8 inches tall, while a 16:10 panel of the same diagonal is taller. Measure your visible screen area, not the bezel, and compare it with the listed dimensions.

A privacy filter narrows the viewing angle so only the person directly in front sees the screen clearly. Side viewers see a dark or blank picture. The narrower the angle, the better the privacy and the dimmer the image straight on, so the right filter is a balance.

Blue-light filters absorb some of the short-wavelength light from a screen and give a warmer tint. They can make a screen feel more comfortable in the evening, but they are not a medical treatment and the effect on eye strain is modest. Look for a stated filter on the listing, and keep expectations realistic.

An anti-glare surface scatters reflections from windows and lights, which helps in bright rooms. A matte finish can slightly soften text, while a glossy filter keeps clarity but shows more reflections. Anti-scratch coatings protect a surface you will touch when cleaning.

Filters attach with adhesive strips, tabs or slide-in brackets, and the method affects how easy they are to reposition. Large sheets can bubble if applied badly, and curved monitors add tension. Check the mounting method on the listing and clean the screen thoroughly before fitting.

howToChoose.intro: Size is the one decision you cannot compromise on, so start by matching the filter to your screen.

faq.q: Will a privacy filter fit my monitor?
faq.a: Only if the filter matches your screen's width, height and aspect ratio. Measure the visible screen area and compare it with the listing, since a 24 inch 16:9 filter will not fit a 24 inch 16:10 monitor. Curved screens need a curved-compatible model like the Mamol 34 Inch.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Buying by diagonal size alone. Two monitors with the same diagonal can have different aspect ratios and dimensions, and a filter that is slightly off will leave a gap or bubble at the edge.

They can make evening screen use feel more comfortable by warming the colors, but the effect on eye strain is modest and they are not a medical treatment. The privacy and glare reduction are the more reliable benefits, so buy for those and treat blue-light filtering as a bonus.

faq.q: How do I install one without bubbles?
faq.a: Clean the screen thoroughly, remove dust with a lint-free cloth and attach the top edge first. Smooth the filter downward slowly to avoid trapping air. Larger sheets such as the 27 inch pair need extra care.

faq.q: How do I clean a privacy filter?
faq.a: Dust it with a dry microfiber cloth, lift smudges with a lightly dampened one and keep solvents away. Anti-scratch coatings like the one on the Mamol help, but any filter can be marked by rough wiping.

faq.q: Will a filter make my screen dim?
faq.a: Yes, every privacy filter reduces brightness and adds some softness, because the film narrows the viewing angle. Raise the monitor brightness a little, and consider a model with anti-glare like the 24 inch anti-glare pair for bright rooms.

finalTake: The Peslv 2-Pack 24 inch privacy screen is the best blue-light-filtering privacy filter for most desks, with strong features in a pair at a mid-range price. Choose the 27 inch pair for larger monitors, the Mamol 34 inch for a curved ultrawide, and the SightPro or 21.5 inch filter for a single screen on a budget. Match size and aspect ratio exactly, and you will get a clean fit and a usable screen.
